summary: Harnett County tower the NC Forest Service built in 1926 as its first lookout; a steel tower replaced the wooden one in 1951. No source describes the site today.

facts.design: Wooden tower with 60-foot juniper corner poles and an 8 x 8 foot glassed cabin, as described in 1926
facts.status_note: No source we found says whether any tower still stands on the site.
facts.agency: North Carolina Division of Forest Resources

events.note: Built in 1925-26 as a 60-foot wooden tower linked by telephone; the Forest Worker reported it complete in September 1926 as the first NC Forest Service lookout tower. Height figures differ (see resolved_conflicts).
100-foot creosoted wood tower erected August 19, 1938. The quoted 1940 report names SCS Camp 18; the page credits the CCC. The sources do not say whether it replaced the 1926 tower.
A steel tower replaced the earlier wood tower.
A dropped Air Force truck landed about 200 feet from the tower while William Holder and his wife were in it, per a Statesville newspaper report quoted on the page.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1925-26 report gives 60 feet and the 1926-28 report gives 65 feet for the wooden tower. The record's 18.3 m matches the 60-foot figure, which is kept.
The page credits the Civilian Conservation Corps, but the quoted 1940 report names SCS Camp 18. The story gives the report's wording and the page's attribution.

notes_for_editor: All history comes from one lookout-history page that quotes state biennial reports (1925-26, 1926-28, 1940), a September 1926 Forest Worker item and a 1965 Statesville newspaper. No primary document was opened. The state list has two Cameron Hill entries; the brief's 'old' coordinates were used, but the sources do not tie the history to either entry. Search returned a DigitalNC photo record titled 'Cameron Hill Tower, Harnett County' (June 1933), which would show a tower by 1933; its page had no readable text and it is not cited. A Mamers fire lookout on Old US 421 near Lillington came up in search but is a different entry (NCT112) and was not used.
